simple: **Inflation** is a general rise in the **price level**. A rise in one good's price is not inflation by itself.
Prices rise when **Aggregate Demand (AD) is bigger than Aggregate Supply (AS)**. Demand-pull pushes AD right; cost-push pushes AS left.
We track a fixed **basket** against a **base year** (index = 100). Inflation is the % change over the **same month** of last year.
India's **headline** inflation is **CPI-C** with a target of **4% ± 2%**. The new **2024 = 100** series has 12 divisions, 358 items and a food weight of 36.75%.
**Core** = headline minus food and fuel. Petrol and diesel stay **inside** core.
Borrowers gain, depositors lose, and the poor are hit hardest (**Engel's Law**). The cure is to **make money expensive**.
terms: One good's price is set by its own demand and supply; the price level is set by AD and AS.
Total demand for all goods and services in the economy.
Total supply of all goods and services that producers make together.
A fixed basket of goods and services for an average person of a target group.
The base-year basket price is set to 100; later baskets are shown against it.
This month against the same month of the previous year.
Overall inflation, measured by CPI-C; the news number.
A few items rise fast while most stay stable.
The rate of inflation falls; prices still rise, only slower.
Low growth, high unemployment and high inflation together.
Inflation pushes people into higher tax brackets, which cools demand by itself.
6.remember: Prices rise when AD beats AS. Measure with a basket and a base year, read headline and core, and cure it by making money expensive.

traps.t: Petrol and diesel are inside core
traps.d: Many assume petrol and diesel sit in 'Fuel and Light'. The handout puts vehicle petrol and diesel under Transport and Communication.
traps.r: Rule: core = headline minus food and fuel (Fuel and Light) only; petrol and diesel come out only in super core.

traps.d: Deflation is a fall in prices. Disinflation is a fall in the rate of inflation; prices still rise, only slower.
traps.r: Rule: prices fall = deflation; the rate falls = disinflation.

traps.d: A rise in the price of one good may cause inflation but is not inflation by itself.
traps.r: Rule: pick the option that says 'general rise' and 'price level'.

traps.d: Two consecutive quarters of falling output is a rule of thumb. The US NBER uses broader metrics to declare a recession.
traps.r: Rule: treat 'two quarters' as the thumb rule, not a legal definition.

traps.d: The fiscal-drag table gives 18.8% for the rise in post-tax income but the text beneath says 18%.
traps.r: Rule: quote about 18.8%; the point is that it is less than 20%.
